message.content: Lions (family Felidae, order Carnivora) and zebras (family Equidae, order Perissodactyla) diverged from a common ancestor that lived roughly 70 million years ago during the Paleocene epoch. That ancestor belonged to the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which later split into the lineages that produced the modern carnivores and the odd‑toed ungulates. In other words, the most recent common ancestor of lions and zebras was a mammal that lived about 70 million years ago and gave rise to the two distinct orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla.
